title: Press a leaning run of books upright and hold it while the other hand slides a book into the 0.7 cm gap
instruction: Put the green book back on the shelf, in the gap beside the books that lean into it: push those books upright and hold them, slide the green book in spine out until its spine is flush with theirs, then let go and move both hands clear.
context: Every home, school and library has a shelf where books have slumped into a gap; library assistants and technicians return books to shelves (O*NET 43-4121.00, 25-4031.00). The hard part is not the insert. The three leaning books do not stand on their own: their cases are racked, so pushed upright and let go they tip back onto the bookend and close the gap (back at 17.5 degrees within 1 s of release). One hand must press the run upright with its fingertips and keep pressing while the other slides a 3.3 cm book into a 0.7 cm fit under them. One hand alone scores 0: in GPU runs the right hand alone, the left hand alone, and the two one after the other all scored 0, because the book cannot enter a leaning run. The hold is scored: from the book entering the gap until it is seated, a fingertip must be pressing on the run at every step, or the score cannot pass 0.5. This is not the reverse of taking a book out of a packed row, where the neighbours stand by themselves.
setup: Rigid parts at real size; positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left), heights above the table. Shelf: an open pine bookcase shelf (a plain pine board shelf, or the top shelf of any open pine bookcase, with the board cut or chosen to this size) standing on the table, board 26 deep x 46 wide, its top 2 cm up, front edge at x 34.5; a 30 cm back panel and a left end panel (inner face y 21.1); open at the right and above. Packed against the end panel: three upright hardcovers (fixed in place; not part of the act). Run: three 6 x 9 in trade hardcovers, 15.2 deep x 22.9 high, 2.6, 3.2 and 3.0 cm thick, 0.55, 0.74 and 0.70 kg, cloth-bound (ordinary used trade hardcovers, 6 x 9 in; any publisher), spines on the line x 35.5, leaning 17 degrees into the gap. They have taken a lean from standing slumped: each case is racked (its boards' tails offset by about a sixth of its thickness, 4.6 to 5.6 mm), so a book stood straight rests on its left board's tail and tips back into the gap; none can stand straight on its own. Bookend: a steel L of 1.2 mm sheet, 0.34 kg, free on the board; plate 14 wide x 13 high standing across the row at y -2.0, base 14 x 13 running under the gap and the run (the books' weight holds it). The end book leans on the plate's top edge: the gap is 4.0 cm at the base and closes to nothing at 13 cm. Green book: a trade hardcover 13.0 deep x 19.5 high x 3.3 thick, 0.55 kg, standing on the table at (25.5, 20), spine toward the robot; 3.5 mm side clearance in the gap, and 1.5 cm between its head and the hold on the end book's head. Friction: cloth 0.4, pine and steel 0.5 (combined by average). Fingers' contact force on the run in the demo (simulator contacts): 2 to 5 N on the way up, about 4 N held (settings, not measurements; any racking that stops the books standing gives the same task). Run limit 1,800 steps (90 s at 20 Hz). Real trial, making the run lean: ordinary hardcovers stand if left alone, so make each one racked. Slip a 5 mm strip of stiff material (5 mm foam board, balsa or plywood), 15 mm wide and 150 mm long, under the tail of the book's left board (the lower back edge of its left cover, at the foot of the case), taped in place, so the case tilts back. Check: stood upright on the shelf and released, each of the three tips back onto the bookend within a second; if one stands, thicken its strip in 1 mm steps. The simulation uses a 10 degree shear of each case in place of the strips (boards' tails offset 4.6 to 5.6 mm). No special books are needed.
scoring: Read with a ruler across the spines, a protractor, a tape mark under the bookend and photos; the rest and the hold need the video. Counted once nothing has moved for 1 s, then at rest 2 s with both hands 3 cm or more from every book and the bookend; until then 0. Score 0 if a run book has fallen at any time (over 35 degrees or off the shelf) or is not in place (spine within 15 mm of the line, across the row within 1 cm of its slot, allowing its lean), or the bookend moved 6 mm, turned 5 degrees or tilted 4 degrees. Else the highest rung: 0.25 green book on the shelf in the gap, 3 cm in, tilted under 35 degrees; 0.5 half its 13 cm depth in; 0.75 spine square to the shelf within 6 degrees and flush within 10 mm (run spines within 15 mm), green book within 12 degrees and run books within 10 degrees of upright; 1.0 the same within 8 degrees. Above 0.5 needs the hold, kept over the whole insertion: from the green book's fore-edge passing 5 mm beyond the run's spines (entering the gap) until its spine is within 10 mm of theirs (seated), at every step a fingertip of one hand presses on a run book (contact force 0.1 N or more, read from the simulator's contacts; on video, fingers visibly on the books) and every run book is within 10 degrees of upright. One step without it and the score stays at 0.5 or less for the rest of the trial; being near the run does not count. A seated book with no such hold scores 0.5 at most; in GPU runs one hand alone never got the book in and scored 0.
reset_notes: Stand the three run books back at 17 degrees on the bookend's top edge, set the green book on its mark, and put the bookend on its tape mark.
fidelity: Rigid-body physics at 240 Hz on GPU. The racking that makes the books tip back is modelled as a 10 degree shear of each case (boards' tails offset 4.6 to 5.6 mm); a real trial uses ordinary hardcovers with a 5 mm x 15 mm x 150 mm strip taped under each left board's tail (see setup). The fingers' contact force on the run is read from the simulator, not measured. Cloth friction 0.4, pine and steel 0.5.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (valid run, 1,800 steps, no session loss); demo: 1.0
